cognitiveEvaluationTheory.title: Cognitive Evaluation Theory (CET)
cognitiveEvaluationTheory.description: Explains the relationship between internal motivation and external rewards
cognitiveEvaluationTheory.keyInsight: When external rewards are controlling, when they pressure individuals to act a certain way, they diminish internal motivation. On the other hand, when external motivations are informational and provide feedback about behaviors, they increase internal motivation.
cognitiveEvaluationTheory.expanseDesign: Expanse rewards are designed to be informational (showing progress, celebrating achievement) rather than controlling (do X to get Y)

competenceResearch.finding: Deci found that giving people unexpected positive feedback on a task increases their intrinsic motivation to do it
competenceResearch.mechanism: Positive feedback fulfilled people's need for competence
competenceResearch.negativeEffect: Vallerand and Reid found negative feedback has the opposite effect (decreasing intrinsic motivation by taking away from people's need for competence)
competenceResearch.implication: Expanse focuses on positive reinforcement and celebrating progress rather than highlighting failures

additionalBenefits.description: SDT influences the fulfillment of meaning-making, well-being, and finding value within internal growth and motivation
additionalBenefits.feedbackEffect: Giving positive feedback on a task served only to increase people's intrinsic motivation and decreased extrinsic motivation for the task

overjustificationEffect.title: Overjustification Effect
overjustificationEffect.definition: A psychological phenomenon where providing excessive external rewards for a behavior that is already intrinsically motivating can lead to a reduction in the intrinsic motivation to perform that behavior.
overjustificationEffect.explanation: When people are given extrinsic rewards (like money, prizes, or praise) for activities they naturally find enjoyable or fulfilling, their internal desire to engage in those activities may diminish.

managingStrategies.description: Foster environments where intrinsic rewards, like personal growth and satisfaction, are emphasized
Provide extrinsic rewards that complement rather than overshadow intrinsic motivations
Offer recognition and praise in a way that supports rather than replaces intrinsic motivation, such as acknowledging effort and improvement

overjustificationEffect.expanseDesign: Expanse is designed with awareness of this effect - rewards enhance rather than replace the natural satisfaction of learning and achievement

negativityBias.title: Negativity Bias
negativityBias.definition: A psychological phenomenon where humans have a tendency to notice and give weight to negative experiences or information over positive ones.
negativityBias.research: Research indicates that humans do have a tendency towards negativity, often referred to as the 'negativity bias'
negativityBias.implication: Educational environments must actively counteract this bias with deliberate positive reinforcement
negativityBias.expanseApproach: Expanse emphasizes positive feedback, celebration of achievements, and constructive rather than critical responses to counteract students' natural negativity bias
